t: #3840 House Robber V — DP with Color-Aware Prefix Best
o: Classic house robber, except adjacency is forbidden only when the two neighboring houses share a color. So when deciding to rob house i, we may build on the best plan ending anywhere up to i-2, and additionally on plans ending at i-1 itself if colors[i] != colors[i-1]. Keeping a prefix maximum pref[i] = max(dp[0..i]) lets each transition be O(1). Verify on example 3: [10,1,3,9], colors [1,1,1,2] gives 10 + 3 + 9 = 22 by robbing 0, 2, 3 (houses 2 and 3 differ in color).
k: dp[i] = nums[i] + max(pref[i-2], and pref[i-1] if colors[i] != colors[i-1]).
pref[i] = max(dp[0..i]) makes each step O(1), giving O(n) overall.
All amounts are positive, so the answer is simply pref[n-1].

a.n: Approach 1: Linear DP with prefix maxima
a.i: Process houses left to right. Robbing house i forbids only house i-1 when colors match; otherwise house i-1 being robbed is fine. The prefix-max array captures 'best plan among houses 0..j', covering both the i-2 and (color-permitting) i-1 cases uniformly.
s: For i >= 1: candidate = nums[i] + pref[i-2] (or nums[i] if i < 2).
If colors[i] != colors[i-1], candidate = max(candidate, nums[i] + pref[i-1]).
Set dp[i] = candidate, pref[i] = max(pref[i-1], dp[i]); answer is pref[n-1].
a.t: O(n) — one pass with O(1) transitions.
a.sp: O(n) for dp and prefix arrays (reducible to O(1) with rolling variables).

w: The trap is assuming the classic robber recurrence still holds — same-colored adjacent houses change the reachable predecessor set. Test on runs of equal colors (degenerates toward classic robber with gaps) and alternating colors (allows near-dense robbing). Follow-ups: circular street, or 'cannot rob three consecutive houses regardless of color'.
